Principal’s Welcome
Welcome to Mulberry Academy London Dock. We’re a vibrant and ambitious school community in the heart of Wapping, just along from Tower Bridge and the City of London.
We opened in September 2024 with our founding cohort of Year 7 students and will grow as a school over the next seven years. Our aim is to ensure outstanding achievement for all, enabling our young people to lead successful and fulfilling lives, making a positive contribution to their own community and beyond. We believe in an education of possibilities, championing children and their families in all that we do.

PSHE
At Mulberry Academy London Dock, Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Education is a vital part of our curriculum and school culture. PSHE equips students with the knowledge, skills and values they need to lead safe, healthy, respectful and fulfilling lives, both now and in the future.
We are committed to delivering a high-quality PSHE curriculum that reflects the diverse experiences of our students and prepares them for life in modern Britain and an increasingly interconnected world. Through PSHE, students develop the confidence, resilience and understanding needed to make informed decisions, build positive relationships and contribute meaningfully to society.
Our PSHE curriculum
Our PSHE curriculum is carefully planned and tailored to each year group, ensuring that content is age-appropriate, relevant and responsive to students’ needs. We follow a spiral curriculum model, revisiting key themes throughout students’ time at the school with increasing depth and complexity. This approach enables students to build upon prior learning, deepen their understanding over time and apply their knowledge to real-life situations as they grow and mature.
PSHE is taught weekly and is structured around the three core themes identified by the Department for Education:
We also respond to local, national and global events through assemblies, form time activities and themed enrichment opportunities, ensuring that learning remains relevant, engaging and empowering.
Health and Wellbeing
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE)
What students learn
Through PSHE, students develop the knowledge and skills to:
Build healthy, respectful and positive relationships
Understand consent, personal boundaries and online safety
Manage mental health, wellbeing and emotional resilience
Understand citizenship, democracy and participation in society
How PSHE is taught
We create a safe, inclusive and respectful learning environment where students are encouraged to ask questions, explore ideas and express their views with confidence and consideration for others.
PSHE is delivered through a range of experiences, including weekly PSHE lessons on a Monday morning with Form Tutors, assemblies, form time activities, enrichment days, guest speakers, workshops and community projects. Students also benefit from careers education and guidance throughout their time at the academy, including opportunities to engage with external providers, employers and higher education institutions.
Our curriculum draws upon high-quality resources and follows national best practice to ensure students receive engaging, accurate and meaningful learning experiences.
Supporting Personal Development
PSHE plays a central role in supporting students’ wider personal development. It complements our pastoral programme and helps students develop the character, confidence and social awareness needed to flourish both within school and beyond.
Through PSHE, students are encouraged to become active citizens who understand their rights and responsibilities, respect diversity and contribute positively to their communities. The programme supports our commitment to promoting wellbeing, equality, inclusion and the fundamental values of democracy, respect, tolerance, individual liberty and the rule of law.
Working in partnership with families
We recognise that PSHE is most effective when schools and families work together. Parents and carers play an important role in supporting young people’s personal development, and we are committed to working in partnership with our community to ensure that our curriculum reflects the needs and values of our students and their families.

pageCache.pageTitle: Smartphone free – Mulberry Academy London Dock
pageCache.text:
Smartphone free
From September 2026, no student at Mulberry Academy London Dock will be permitted to bring a smartphone or smart device onto the school site. This policy will apply to all year groups.
A smart device, means any electronic device capable of accessing the internet, including smartphones and smartwatches, regardless of whether they are marketed as ‘restricted’ or ‘locked down’. All smart devices will be treated as prohibited items and confiscated in accordance with our behaviour policy if seen or heard on site.
Students may bring a basic call-and-text phone if required for their journey to and from school. Our ‘No See, No Hear’ will remain the same. These devices must:
From September 2026, a student found with a smartphone or smart device on site will have it confiscated for 10 school days, will be internally excluded for a day, and a parent or carer will be required to meet with the Principal to collect it at the end of the tenth day. If this should happen again, there will be further sanctions accordingly, and the phone will be confiscated for a longer period of time.
A student whose permitted basic phone is switched on or visible during the school day will receive a 90 minute detention, and have their phone confiscated for 2 days. A parent or carer will be required to meet with a member of senior staff to collect the phone at the end of the second day. If this should happen again, there will be further sanctions accordingly, and the phone will be confiscated for a longer period of time.
Why is Mulberry Academy London Dock smartphone free?
We have listened closely to the views of our own school community, as well as the changing picture both locally and nationally. Many of our students don’t have a mobile phone, and a significant number also have basic call and text phones.
The skills that we believe will carry our students furthest, including communication, empathy, critical thinking, and resilience, are developed through real experience and real relationships. Being smartphone-free, gives students the space to build develop and grow without the added pressures of social comparison or pull of a screen. This is not a step away from technology. Our students engage with digital tools regularly as part of their learning, and we remain committed to developing their digital literacy and online awareness throughout their time at the school.
We want our students to be safe on their way to and from school, and it can often be assumed that a smartphone is the best way to ensure that. However, smartphones don’t just offer connection, they also open the door to harmful content, group chats, and pressure to respond at all hours. Even with good intentions, they can expose young people to things they’re simply not ready for. There’s also a growing issue with phone theft. Around 500 children are mugged for their phones every day in the UK (ONS, 2019), and many secondary students admit to using their phones while walking, leading to accidents and near-misses. We understand that tracking can offer reassurance to families. Devices like Airtags are a great alternative, they’re affordable, discreet, and far less likely to be lost or stolen.
A simple brick phone (call and text only) is more than enough for emergencies or last-minute changes, and in many ways, it makes a child’s journey safer, not riskier.
Safety and communication
We understand that many families feel reassured by knowing their child can reach them. A basic call-and-text device gives families that peace of mind without the risks that come with internet-enabled devices. Our policy actively supports student safety by reducing exposure to safeguarding risks during the school day and on the journey home.
If you need to contact your child during the school day, our school office is your first point of contact and messages will be passed on. If your child needs to reach you, they can do so through the office at any time.

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values – Mulberry Academy London Dock
pageCache.text:
British Values
At Mulberry Academy London Dock, we are committed to preparing students to be responsible, respectful and active citizens who make a positive contribution to their local community, wider British society and the global community. We promote the fundamental British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
We recognise that these values are not only British values but are also shared global values that help people live together peacefully, respectfully and successfully in diverse societies around the world. Through our curriculum and wider school experiences, students develop the knowledge, skills and understanding needed to become thoughtful, informed and compassionate members of society.
The promotion of British Values is embedded throughout school life and is closely linked to our commitment to students’ Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural (SMSC) development. Students learn about fairness, equality, human rights, diversity and social responsibility through lessons, assemblies, tutor time, leadership opportunities and enrichment activities.
We encourage students to use their voice, engage in debate, respect different viewpoints and understand the importance of participating positively in democratic society. Students are supported to develop confidence, resilience and independence, while learning to value and celebrate the diverse backgrounds, cultures and experiences that make up our school community.
These values are also brought to life through our enrichment experiences, educational visits, residential trips and our extensive Wonder 7 after-school programme. Opportunities such as Model United Nations, the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award, and Debate Mate help students develop leadership skills, confidence, public speaking and teamwork, while encouraging them to engage thoughtfully with local, national and global issues.
Students also benefit from the wide range of opportunities offered through the Mulberry Schools Trust Changemaker Programmes, including Global Girl Leading, the Mulberry STEM Academy and the Mulberry Production Arts Academy. Through participation in the Mulberry Festival of Arts and the Rightful Place Arts Conference, students are encouraged to explore creativity, social justice, equality and civic responsibility.
Through these experiences, students develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to make a positive contribution to their communities and gain a deeper understanding of their role in creating a fairer, more inclusive and sustainable world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision, Mission and Values – Mulberry Academy London Dock
pageCache.text:
Our Vision, Mission and Values
Vision
Our vision is to create an education of endless possibilities, inspiring curiosity, empowering every student to achieve excellence
Mission
Our mission is to build a vibrant, ambitious and inclusive school community where our pursuit of excellence underpins high achievement, and where every child is known, valued and championed as an individual. Guided by our values of Diligence, Open‑Mindedness, Citizenship and Kindness, we deliver high‑quality teaching, enriching learning experiences and exceptional pastoral care. Working in partnership with families, our local community and the Mulberry Schools Trust, we set the highest expectations and ensure every student has the best possible chance to succeed.
Values
We place our community at the heart of everything we do, building strong partnerships with families and working together to support every child’s success.
We have high aspirations, inspiring curiosity, determination and pride in learning for all students.
We value every child as an individual, ensuring each student is known, respected and championed to fulfil their potential.
We live our values of Diligence, Open‑Mindedness, Citizenship and Kindness, shaping learners who contribute positively and confidently to the world around them.
We do this together, united by a shared commitment to excellence and a belief in the limitless potential of every child.
We strive for excellence, continuous improvement and impeccable behaviour, which defines our approach to learning and personal growth.
We are hardworking. We are responsible. We are ambitious.
We participate as active scholars.
We focus on our tasks with determination, working steadily towards our personal and academic goals.
We persevere through challenges.
We tackle difficulties with a positive attitude, learning from mistakes and trying again.
We are open-minded in our pursuit of knowledge, taking risks in our learning and the exploration of new ideas.
We are inquisitive. We are creative. We are resilient.
We listen and respect different viewpoints.
We consider and value diverse opinions, understanding that others may think differently.
We embrace learning beyond the classroom.
We show curiosity and a desire to learn by investigating new ideas and asking thoughtful questions.
We are responsible and active citizens who contribute positively to our communities and the world around us.
We show integrity. We show respect. We show loyalty.
We act responsibly and help our community.
We take responsibility for our actions and contribute positively to our classroom, school, and local community.
We follow rules and show respect for others.
We adhere to guidelines that ensure a safe and respectful environment for everyone.
We place kindness, empathy and compassion at the heart of our school, fostering a culture of respect and inclusivity.
We show empathy. We show tolerance. We show courtesy.
We celebrate our differences and care about each other.
We try to understand the feelings of others and act with kindness to support them.
We include and support everyone.
We make an effort to include others and offer help and encouragement to those who need it.
